analysis.investment_thesis: Chalet Hotels is a capital-intensive, cyclical lodging business with a paltry 5.77% ROE that does not meet my minimum threshold of 15% — shareholders are not being rewarded for the capital deployed. At 28x P/E with negative free cash flow in 2025 (capex surged to INR 969 Cr) and a history littered with net losses (six of ten years), the price demands perfection that this business cannot reliably deliver.
key_strengths: Strong and expanding operating margins (35.5%) and EBITDA CAGR of 14% over 9 years indicate real operating leverage in the hotel portfolio
Revenue has recovered sharply post-COVID, reaching INR 1,718 Cr in 2025 — a 9Y CAGR of 12.8% — showing brand relevance in upper-upscale segment
Borrowings actually declined from INR 3,005 Cr to INR 2,489 Cr in 2025 alongside a large equity raise, improving the balance sheet
key_risks: ROE of only 5.77% on INR 3,415 Cr of equity is economically destructive; hotel real estate eats capital without commensurate returns
Free cash flow turned negative in 2025 (-INR 14 Cr) as capex exploded to INR 969 Cr — the business is in heavy investment mode with uncertain payback
Cyclicality is proven and brutal: revenue crashed from INR 981 Cr (2020) to INR 286 Cr (2021) and the company burned cash for three consecutive years
red_flags: Net profit has been negative in six out of ten fiscal years — this is not a durable earnings machine
D/E of 0.73 in a highly cyclical, capital-intensive business leaves little cushion in downturns
Capex jumped 122% year-on-year to INR 969 Cr in 2025 with investing outflows of INR 1,355 Cr — capital allocation discipline is questionable
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Chalet Hotels exemplifies the type of business I actively avoid: it requires constant capital infusions to grow, earns mediocre returns on that capital, and is beholden to macroeconomic cycles. A 5.77% ROE tells me management has not earned the right to deploy more capital, yet they are aggressively doing so. The hotel industry has no lasting moat — a new Marriott or Hilton property nearby can immediately erode occupancy and pricing power.

The valuation of 28x P/E on volatile, historically loss-prone earnings offers no margin of safety. While operating margins look attractive at 35%, heavy depreciation, finance costs, and now accelerating capex consume the economic profits. The large equity raise in 2025 (equity jumped INR 1.56 lakh Cr) diluted shareholders to fund expansion — I want management allocating profits, not continuously seeking new capital.
